newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel, PLO to move talks to Red Sea resorts.
newsitem.headline: Israel, PLO to move talks to Red Sea resorts.

text.p: Israel and the PLO have decided to move their negotiations from the Gaza Strip to the Red Sea resorts of Eilat, in Israel, and Taba, in Egypt from Monday, a U.S. mediator said on Thursday.

"The parties agreed that in order to make continuous, to intensify and to accelerate their discussions, the various committees would begin meeting on Monday, October 14 on a rotating basis in Taba and Eilat," U.S. Special Mideast Coordinator Dennis Ross said in a statement.

Spurred by a White House summit after Israeli-Palestinian clashes last month in the West Bank and Gaza, negotiations began on Sunday on how to implement a long-delayed Israeli troop redeployment from the West Bank city of Hebron.

Israel wants to increase security for 400 Jewish settlers in Hebron, home to 100,000 Palestinians, but has insisted it was not reopening a partial pullout accord the previous Labour-led government signed with the PLO.

In the statement, Ross said: "Both sides agreed that they are not reopening or renegotiating the agreement and that they are discussing the mechanisms and the modalities for how best to implement the agreement."
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told legislators in self-ruled Ramallah, in the West Bank, on Thursday that the negotiations had yet to make progress.
